item.title: A 27-year-old AI researcher quit Anthropic, fearing AI could cause human extinction
item.description: Jacob Coxon, a 27-year-old Cambridge-trained researcher and GPT-4.5 core contributor, quit Anthropic after stints in frontier pretraining at OpenAI and Anthropic, warning that labs are racing toward self-improving superintelligence and betting with human lives—his post blew past 100M views on X. Anthropic’s alignment lead and other insiders backed him personally, putting extinction odds this decade above 10%. Kazike rereads Tim Urban’s 2015 AI Revolution—exponential progress, the intelligence ladder, extinction vs species immortality—and feels we are already on that timeline; he hopes the balance beam tips toward immortality.

item.title: @Xudong07452910 · LLMs as Cognitive Viruses: Tipping Point, Hysteresis & Cognitive Immunity
item.description: Treats LLMs as “cognitive viruses” and models adoption with epidemic dynamics. Three states—independent, assisted-but-independent, persistently dependent—can tip past a threshold into mass cognitive outsourcing, with hysteresis that makes recovery harder than prevention. Distinguishes scaffold (extend judgment) vs substitute (outsource judgment) and proposes cognitive immunity: keep some reading, writing, reasoning, and verification without AI.

item.title: GitHub 3.2万 Star，又一款国产的顶级 Agent 记忆系统火了！

item.title: Claude Formalizes Fermat's Last Theorem in 11 Days — Yao Class Alum Leads
item.description: Anthropic reports Claude nearly autonomously completed the first end-to-end Lean formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem in about 11 days—roughly 13M lines of Lean and 29.5k intermediate theorems. Led by Tsinghua Yao Class alum Tianyi Peng with multi-agent Claude and Prove2Me. The point is machine-checkable formalization of a human proof, addressing how hard it is to verify complex mathematics.

item.title: @python_xxt · The right way to open GPT-6 Astra (systemic diagnosis prompt)
item.description: - 基于过去的对话、经历、能力和风险偏好，对用户进行系统性诊断并提供可执行建议。 - 找出关键的 3–5 项瓶颈、风险和机会，重点揭示用户未意识到的盲点并指出需立即停止的行为。 - 为每条核心建议说明重要性、适配原因、具体执行步骤以及不执行的代价，并给出 30 天、90 天和 1 年的行动重点。 - 若只能做一项改变，明确指出最关键的改变，并提供未来 3 年的主线方向和决策原则。

item.title: How to turn your AI into a world-class designer
item.description: Former Apple AI product design R&D lead Anshu Chimala explains how to push AI past generic design. LLMs as next-token predictors default to safe, crowd-pleasing choices—the opposite of great design's emotional surprise. He reframes Double Diamond for agents: Discover (seed strings for variety, ambitious prompts), Define (critic subagents, image/video gen for identity), Deliver (subtract ruthlessly, remove AI tells). The gap isn't the model—it's whether you steer taste. Cheap implementers + strong critics + media tools raise quality without exploding cost.

item.title: @Xudong07452910 · After 70 Coding-Agent Rounds: Harness-of-Harness
item.description: - Harness-of-Harness organizes coding frameworks like Codex, OpenCode, and Pi into a cyclic iterative development flow; each round includes planning, implementation, and independent QA acceptance. - Across 70 development rounds, 81 issues were recorded and 65 closed; 17 issues reappeared due to later changes, showing regression. - Experiments show HoH improves ~52.25% on average vs. standalone frameworks across three benchmarks; on FrontierSWE, Codex + GPT-5.5 rose from 22% to 72.67%. - The key for long-running coding agents is preserving verified progress and preventing new features from reintroducing old bugs—engineering continuity.

item.title: @xuanyuanzhifeng · Understand Transformer in One Go
item.description: - This article systematically introduces Transformer core concepts, including attention, QKV, residual connections, and other key techniques. - Self-Attention enables global information exchange among tokens, solving RNN/LSTM long-range dependency and sequential computation issues. - Multi-head attention, positional encoding, feed-forward networks, and residual connections together form Transformer's basic unit, enabling efficient parallel training while preserving sequence order. - The encoder-decoder structure plus masked self-attention and cross-attention let the model understand input text and avoid leaking future information when generating output.

item.title: @Zen_with_AI · Why KV Cache Stores Only K/V, Not Q
item.description: - During autoregressive generation, only the current Q is dotted with all historical K, then used to weight all V, so only K and V need to be cached. - Under causal masking, historical K/V do not change with new tokens and can be reused directly, avoiding recomputation. - The Q produced at each step is used only in that step and is not needed next, so Q is not stored. - Each step only recomputes Q, K, and V for the new position and writes the new K/V into the cache.

item.title: @Xudong07452910 · SKILLSTATE: Keep Only Current State
item.description: - Long-running Agents should keep only "current state": each step uses only a fixed Skill, the current structured state, and the latest observation, then discards intermediate reasoning. - SKILLSTATE cuts token use from about 1.06M to 65K (~16× reduction) and raises accuracy from 0.91 to 0.94. - On InterCode CTF and τ-Bench benchmarks, SKILLSTATE both improves success rate and significantly reduces token use. - The takeaway: treat long-term context as continuously updated working state—forget completed steps and keep only what remains useful.

item.title: Users and Revenue Aren't Enough: AI Apps Still Aren't a Good Business
item.description: - AI apps face three major challenges: rapid model iteration swallowing features, growth that is hard to monetize, and user entry points controlled upstream. - High growth often comes with high costs; many AI companies lose money after scaling users, with gross margins generally low or even negative. - To counter model cannibalization, founders can shift to vertical niches with delivery services, train their own models, or boost competitiveness via open source. - Only by delivering profitable outcomes downstream or building models upstream do AI application companies have higher survival odds.

item.title: AGI Hunt · Chain-of-Experience: Don't Rush to Compress Attempt History
item.description: - Research found that retaining complete attempt history and feedback signals can raise average model accuracy to 71.0%. - Iterative solving without feedback achieves 66.8% accuracy; with external feedback it can reach 79.3%. - Although context is longer, convergence is faster, overall token consumption drops by about 19%, and API costs decrease. - For Agent context management, this reminds us not to rush to compress history—sometimes keeping more information is more effective.

item.title: 5 Million Views: AI Builds an "Infinite Slop" Machine
item.description: - Infinite Slop is an endlessly looping AI-generated video livestream site where viewers type prompts in chat and AI generates short clips in real time for continuous playback. - It uses the Fal platform's H3 Max model; a 15-second video takes about 9 seconds to generate, so generation outpaces playback. - The system maintains coherence via audience voting, prompt expansion, and parallel generation, but quality varies and often yields "slop"-like low-quality content. - 24/7 continuous operation costs about $207,000 per month, sparking dual discussions on AI content proliferation and innovation.
